tagline: Internal finance in one place: customer retainers and their payments, your own subscriptions, and the software vendors you pay for.
summary: Finances Manager tracks the money side of a small studio. **Retainers** are monthly billables per customer, with a due day and a payment log; **subscriptions** are the recurring spend you pay out, linked to an **external software** vendor catalog. A finances dashboard brings the three together.

It was split out of My Ops Tracker: finance tables moved from ops-tracker's Supabase into this project's own Postgres, while customers stay in the ops-tracker CRM. The API has no database of its own — it calls a storage server directly or through the studio gateway — and reads customer names through a CRM proxy. My Ops Tracker can, in turn, reach these finance routes via its `/api/finances-remote` proxy.
audience: You run a studio or agency with monthly retainer customers and want to see who has paid.
You want a clear list of every SaaS subscription the business pays for and what it costs.
Your customers already live in My Ops Tracker.
notFor: Accounting, invoicing or bank sync — it records retainers, payments and subscriptions; it doesn't send invoices or reconcile accounts.
Managing customers — they're read from My Ops Tracker.
Running without the storage server — the API can't reach Postgres itself.

capabilities.title: Finances dashboard
capabilities.detail: `/finances` summarizes retainers, subscriptions and software spend.

capabilities.title: Customer retainers
capabilities.detail: `/finances/retainers` and `/customer-retainer-detail-page`: monthly amount and due day per customer, plus a payment log (`retainer_payments`).

capabilities.title: Subscriptions
capabilities.detail: `/finances/subscriptions`: recurring internal spend with schedule validation, linked to a vendor.

capabilities.title: External software
capabilities.detail: `/finances/software`: the vendor catalog subscriptions point to.

capabilities.title: CRM-aware
capabilities.detail: Customer names come from My Ops Tracker via `/api/crm/*`; the API can check a customer exists before saving a retainer.

components.name: Web app
components.owns: Dashboard, retainers, subscriptions and software screens. Calls the API at `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`.

components.name: API
components.owns: `/api/data/*` for external software, subscriptions, customer retainers and retainer payments, business rules (schedules, due days, payment sources), and the `/api/crm/*` proxy.
components.doesNotOwn: SQL — every CRUD call goes to storage `invoke`.

components.name: Storage server
components.doesNotOwn: CRM foreign keys — customer ids are logical references only.

components.name: Project dispatcher
components.owns: `dispatcher.services.json` / `dispatcher.projects.json` for the main gateway. The runtime still has to be copied from code-commit-summaries' dispatcher.

dataFlow: The web app calls the finances API at `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`.
The API invokes storage: **direct** (`FINANCES_MANAGER_STORAGE_URL` + secret) or **gateway** (`CANONICAL_DATA_ACCESS_MODE=gateway` with `FINANCES_MANAGER_GATEWAY_*`).
Storage runs the SQL against local Postgres `finances_manager`.
Customer names: the API forwards `GET /api/crm/*` to ops-tracker's `/api/data/*` (`OPS_TRACKER_EXPRESS_URL`, optional service secret).
My Ops Tracker can read and write finance data through its `/api/finances-remote` proxy to this API.

trust.title: API
trust.detail: Holds the storage secret and the ops-tracker service secret. No `DATABASE_URL`.

trust.title: Storage host
trust.detail: Only place with `DATABASE_URL`; accepts callers with `STORAGE_DISPATCHER_SECRET`.

trust.title: My Ops Tracker
trust.detail: Source of customers; can call this API with `x-finances-manager-service-secret`.

commonTasks.title: Run on one machine
steps: On the **Storage Express** repo, **Set up local database** to create `finances_manager` and apply `migrations/001…006`.
Fix the storage `.env`: `PORT=3091` and `DATABASE_URL=…/finances_manager` (the example was copied from estimate-and-proposals).
Set `STORAGE_DISPATCHER_SECRET` on storage and the same value as `FINANCES_MANAGER_STORAGE_SECRET` on the API; set `OPS_TRACKER_EXPRESS_URL`.

commonTasks.title: Move finance data out of ops-tracker
steps: Apply storage migrations on the target database.
Export from ops-tracker Supabase in order: `external_software`, `subscriptions`, `customer_retainers`, `retainer_payments`, keeping the UUIDs.

commonTasks.title: Record a retainer payment
steps: Add a payment with amount, date and source.

troubleshooting.symptom: Storage starts on 3081 or connects to `estimate_and_proposals`
troubleshooting.fix: The storage `.env.example` was copied from estimate-and-proposals. Set `PORT=3091` and `DATABASE_URL` to `finances_manager`.
The CRM proxy can't reach ops-tracker. Check `OPS_TRACKER_EXPRESS_URL` and `OPS_TRACKER_SERVICE_SECRET`. Finance CRUD still works.

troubleshooting.symptom: Saving a retainer fails with an unknown customer
troubleshooting.fix: The customer id doesn't exist in My Ops Tracker.

glossary.definition: A customer's recurring monthly billable, with a due day and payments.
Recurring spend the business pays to a vendor.
Vendor catalog entry that subscriptions reference.
My Ops Tracker's proxy route into this API.

hubNotes: Most of the code isn't committed yet — each repo has a single "Initial commit" and a large set of uncommitted changes (web: 200+ source files on disk vs 9 tracked).
Port clashes in the registry: this project's web port 3093 is also estimate-and-proposals' dispatcher port, and the dispatcher README here uses 3095, which is estimate-and-proposals' API port.
`finances-manager-dispatcher-express-server` is in the registry but has no path in hub.local.json and no runtime yet.
The ops-tracker CRM URL defaults to `http://localhost:3009`, the same port several other projects use.
